assets.prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing
Asset type: project launch hero, README cover, presentation opening slide.
Create one finished promotional image for the real open-source software project Intentum. Use the built-in image generator to produce a raster image, wide landscape 16:9, ideally 2560 x 1440 or higher, with all content comfortably inside the canvas. A coordinated visual direction for this series: midnight navy background, restrained luminous teal/cyan signal paths, soft ivory typography and occasional warm amber highlights; sophisticated editorial typography, precise alignment, generous negative space, very fine engineering-grid details, exquisite shallow 3D glass and brushed-metal accents. This is art-directed technical communication for developers and researchers: beautiful, calm, highly readable, not noisy cyberpunk. Use only the specified text. No watermarks, invented metrics, benchmark scores, brand logos of other products, robot mascots or extra copy. Spell the project name exactly Intentum (I-n-t-e-n-t-u-m).
Primary request: A striking launch visual expressing a probabilistic agent's loose semantic intent becoming structured, deterministic data operations.
Composition: an editorial cover with a large, beautifully typeset Intentum wordmark and short supporting statement in the left upper portion, balanced by a luminous architectural object across the central and right portion. Leave generous air around the type. The sculptural object is a refined, translucent rectangular gateway standing on a very subtle grid plane. Fine curved signal strands and a handful of loosely arranged translucent abstract data fragments approach the gateway from the left. Passing through it, they become several impeccably aligned, parallel light paths and crisp tabular grids exiting to the right. A sense of transformation from loose references to structured execution, without showing a human brain or an AI robot. An amber focal glow at the gateway, teal glass edges, photorealistic material rendering with elegant controlled bloom; keep all lettering flat and sharp.
Text, verbatim:
Largest title: "Intentum"
Supporting statement on two lines: "Semantic intent." and "Deterministic data operations."
Small eyebrow: "AGENT-READY DATA BACKEND"
Three compact feature labels along the bottom: "Typed operations", "Inspectable plans", "Traceable results"
Accuracy: represent a general data backend prototype. This image must not claim that an agent's interpretation is always correct, that the system is production-certified, or that it guarantees task accuracy.
Avoid: dense diagrams, paragraph text, stock-tech globe, excessive bloom, generic AI brains, fake UI screenshots. Make this a memorable premium project cover.

Use case: infographic-diagram
Asset type: promotional software architecture diagram for README and technical presentations.
Create one finished promotional image for the real open-source software project Intentum. Use the built-in image generator to produce a raster image, wide landscape 16:9, ideally 2560 x 1440 or higher, with all content comfortably inside the canvas. A coordinated visual direction for this series: midnight navy background, restrained luminous teal/cyan signal paths, soft ivory typography and occasional warm amber highlights; sophisticated editorial typography, precise alignment, generous negative space, very fine engineering-grid details, exquisite shallow 3D glass and brushed-metal accents. This is art-directed technical communication for developers and researchers: beautiful, calm, highly readable, not noisy cyberpunk. Use only the specified text. No watermarks, invented metrics, benchmark scores, brand logos of other products, robot mascots or extra copy. Spell the project name exactly Intentum (I-n-t-e-n-t-u-m).
Primary request: A precise, gorgeous layered architecture view of Intentum, with readable flat typography and restrained 3D diagram surfaces. Place the diagram across most of the frame, beneath a clean title area. The diagram is the subject, not a tiny diagram inside a decorative scene. Layer alignment and spacing must make the boundaries obvious.
Text and layout, verbatim:
Header: "Intentum" and "System architecture"
At the top, a wide clearly separate panel labeled "Agent harness"; secondary text "Host adapters · Optional perception · Measurement". This panel is OUTSIDE the backend. It stands for the agent side.
A single prominent bidirectional connector between this top panel and the backend is labeled "MCP tools". Calls and structured responses pass through this one boundary.
Middle: a large elegant outlined panel labeled "Intentum backend". Inside, a left-to-right connected row of exactly six small equally weighted stages, in this exact order:
"Resolve" → "Canonical IR" → "Validate" → "Plan" → "Execute" → "Commit"
Below this row, still inside the backend panel, four secondary capability chips, not pipeline steps:
"Output contracts" | "Recovery advice" | "Lineage + audit" | "Idempotent replay"
Bottom: three separate sibling storage panels under the backend, each with its own downward connector from the backend, never one database flowing into the next:
"DuckDB" with subtitle "Analytical tables"
"SQLite" with subtitle "Metadata + operations"
"Managed files" with subtitle "Imported sources"
Visual style: extremely clear system diagram, luminous thin connectors, small arrowheads, softly rounded glass panels, clean ivory modern sans-serif text, mild amber accent for the MCP boundary and teal for the backend. Use a small table icon, metadata ledger icon, and file-stack icon for the three storage panels. No vendor logos.
Architecture invariants: the agent harness and optional perception are outside the deterministic backend; no direct agent-to-storage connection. Files and stores are real persistence choices, not aspirational PostgreSQL or cloud components. No model, perception module or benchmark scorer inside the backend. Six pipeline stages must appear exactly once in the correct order. All text must be comfortably legible and spelled exactly. Diagram should be polished and enticing but accurate.

Use case: infographic-diagram
Asset type: promotional execution-flow diagram for technical presentations and project documentation.
Create one finished promotional image for the real open-source software project Intentum. Use the built-in image generator to produce a raster image, wide landscape 16:9, ideally 2560 x 1440 or higher, with all content comfortably inside the canvas. A coordinated visual direction for this series: midnight navy background, restrained luminous teal/cyan signal paths, soft ivory typography and occasional warm amber highlights; sophisticated editorial typography, precise alignment, generous negative space, very fine engineering-grid details, exquisite shallow 3D glass and brushed-metal accents. This is art-directed technical communication for developers and researchers: beautiful, calm, highly readable, not noisy cyberpunk. Use only the specified text. No watermarks, invented metrics, benchmark scores, brand logos of other products, robot mascots or extra copy. Spell the project name exactly Intentum (I-n-t-e-n-t-u-m).
Primary request: A visually compelling, accurate six-stage flow for the successful transform materialization path in Intentum. It should feel like a beautifully crafted process map, with strong hierarchy and generous spacing.
Top title: "Intentum"
Main headline: "From intent to a committed result"
Small subtitle: "Transform materialization path"
Upper rail, above the process cards: a concise input pill reading "Semantic intent" on the left, associated with stage 01, and an output pill reading "Structured result" on the right, associated with stage 06.
Main composition: exactly six substantial equally spaced cards in ONE horizontal left-to-right row with clear arrows between neighboring cards. Use elegant glass tiles, large understated sequence numbers, sharp flat text and minimalist line icons. Never wrap or reorder the flow. Card contents, verbatim:
01 — "Resolve" / "Bind references"
02 — "Canonical IR" / "Typed operation"
03 — "Validate" / "Check schema + versions"
04 — "Plan" / "Inspectable steps"
05 — "Execute" / "DuckDB materialization"
06 — "Commit" / "SQLite metadata"
Connect input to Resolve and Commit to the result. Cyan light runs continuously through the successful path, with a restrained amber accent at validation and the commit endpoint.
Under the cards, a clean shared evidence band labeled "Lineage · Audit · Idempotency". This is supporting metadata, not another execution stage.
At the bottom, two compact clearly readable annotation panels, independent of the successful path:
"On refusal" with "Structured advice returns to the agent"
"On metadata commit failure" with "Compensate by dropping the new table"
Use a subtle curved return-arrow icon for the refusal annotation, and a rollback icon for the compensation annotation. Do not attach an ambiguous connector between the two annotations.
Factual invariants: canonical IR comes BEFORE validation; planning comes BEFORE execution; metadata commit comes AFTER DuckDB materialization. This is specifically the successful materialized-transform path, not a claim that preview calls commit a dataset. Compensation describes handled metadata-commit failures, not cross-database crash-proof transactions. Refusal advice goes to the agent and does not silently execute an automatic repair. No guarantee of task truth, automatic self-healing, time travel, or unsupported features.
Text should remain legible at presentation size. Prioritize exact labels and arrow order over decoration.
